verdictRationale: V1 is genuinely closed and its falsifiability proof is sufficient; R3 is correctly executed as a behaviour change (monotone, verbatim in the contract, no delta on the measured corpus). But R1's delivery-facing acceptance criteria are unmet by any shipped code path: every R1 primitive has zero call sites (F-1), expiry has no caller and notifies nobody (F-2), 'delivery after approval' exists only as a comment and as a step the QA script performs on itself, R1-4 has no evidence at all (F-5), and the delivered clear primitive will resurrect acknowledged records into the scheduler's auto-delivery path as soon as it is wired (F-3).

acceptanceResults.criterion: 风险清单: most likely regression + executable prevention
acceptanceResults.evidence: F-3 is the named risk with a three-part prevention (filter tombstones in readUnreadMailbox, keep the read/claimed markers, add the seam test 'cleared mailbox => 0 unread, 0 deliverable').

findings.problem: Every R1 primitive is defined and unit-tested but has ZERO call sites in the shipped runtime (tools.js, scheduler.js, members.js, index.js, quality-gates.js, harness-compat.js): appendMailboxDeduped, clearMailboxToWatermark, readLiveMailbox, enqueueInterjection, expireInterjections, readPendingInterjections, readInterjections; decideInterjection's only hit is the JSDoc line scheduler.js:231. The shipped send tool (tools.js:1815) appends with appendMailbox at tools.js:1871/:1887 and does not import appendMailboxDeduped (tools.js:15). Measured: 3 identical sends through the shipped append path = 3 records / 3 unread, i.e. N deliveries. No agent-facing surface can enqueue, decide, clear or expire anything. R1's delivery-facing acceptance criteria (R1-1 operative clause, R1-3 clauses 2 and 3, R1-4) are therefore unmet by the delivered system.
findings.requiredFix: Either (a) wire R1 in this wave: move tools.js:1871/:1887 to appendMailboxDeduped; add the interjection enqueue/decide surface with the frozen clear-authority rule (captain may clear any mailbox, a member only its own); re-post on 'approved' through the existing member-prompt queue seam at the next step boundary (never harness sendMessage-steer); call expireInterjections on the scheduler's idle edge; or (b) record R1-1 (operative clause), R1-3 and R1-4 as NOT MET in the ledger and parent result and open a new task whose inScope names lib/tools.js + lib/scheduler.js. Do not leave them passed.

findings.problem: expireInterjections has no caller, and its own docstring (state.js:643-645) claims 'the requesting member is notified (status expired)' while the function only rewrites status/decidedAt. Measured: after an expiry the requester's inbox holds 0 records. The frozen decision onCaptainSilence requires default DENY + TTL 30 min + notify the requesting member, so a member who asks for permission and gets no answer learns nothing.
findings.requiredFix: Append an ordinary message to record.from inside the expiry path (or in the caller that expires) and drive expireInterjections from a real tick (scheduler idle edge / session start); keep the row-level status:'expired' as is.

findings.problem: clearMailboxToWatermark (state.js:508) rewrites each cleared row as a tombstone that drops readAt/deliveryClaimedAt, while readUnreadMailbox (state.js:717) filters on readAt === undefined and — unlike readLiveMailbox (state.js:544) — does not filter tombstone !== true; the scheduler's two delivery reads (scheduler.js:303, :366) go through readUnreadMailbox + deliverableUnread (scheduler.js:235), which only drops kind === INTERJECTION_KIND. Measured: 2 acknowledged records (0 unread) -> one clear -> 2 unread / 2 deliverable, tombstone keys [id,from,to,content,ts,tombstone,clearedAt,clearedToWatermark,archivedTo]; 3 uncleared records -> 3 deliverable empty-content tombstones. Latent today only because the clear has no caller (F-1); it becomes a storm of empty prompts to already-served members the moment one is wired. It also makes the delivered claim 'after clear the read returns only the tombstone' false for the reader the scheduler actually uses.
findings.requiredFix: Filter tombstone !== true inside readUnreadMailbox (or in deliverableUnread), and do not let a tombstone re-open an acknowledged record (keep readAt, or carry an explicit clearedAt exclusion). Add the seam test 'after a clear: 0 unread, 0 deliverable' to test/r1-message-channel.test.mjs.

findings.problem: decideInterjection writes any decision string verbatim as status. Measured: decision 'banana' -> status 'banana'; the row then leaves readPendingInterjections (state.js:637 filters status==='pending') without being approved or rejected, and a later real decision is refused with 'is already banana'. This is V1's 'returns a value nobody can act on' class relocated to the decision side, and there is no tool layer (F-1) to constrain the argument.
findings.requiredFix: Allow-list {approved, rejected} and reject anything else loudly, naming the allowed values.

findings.problem: The frozen criterion 'duplicate delivery does not double the member's actions (assert the task-update call count does not double on redelivery)' is asserted nowhere: grep for 'call count|callCount|not double|redeliver' over the plugin tests, self-fix tests and the messaging QA case returns 0 hits, so its passed status rests on nothing — and it is unmeasurable while dedup is unwired.
findings.requiredFix: Once F-1(a) lands, assert it at the tool boundary: two identical agent_teams_send_message calls inside the window -> exactly one scheduler delivery and exactly one agent_teams_update_task, recorded as a call count.

findings.problem: The acceptance text reads as 'the durable JSONL still holds all N records folded with dupCount=N', while the shipped primitive keeps ONE record (test/r1-message-channel.test.mjs:55 asserts length === 1; probe confirms 1). The t35 record discloses the real shape, so this is a spec-text divergence rather than a concealed one, but a later auditor reading the criterion literally will fail working code — or 'fix' the primitive to keep N records and re-open the duplicate-delivery path.
findings.requiredFix: Record the operative reading ('at-most-once delivery; one surviving record; N stored in dupCount') as a pin-only wording addendum. Do not change the primitive.

findings.problem: Two transcription gaps in the C row (neither introduced by R3): complexityGate.signals.C_enumeratedSteps.detect transcribes C1 as ^\s*(\d+[.)]|[-*])\s while the shipped pattern (session-start.js:100) is ^\s*(?:\d+[.)]|[-*|])\s (the table-row alternative is missing), and the C3 prose says clauses 'each pair an action verb with an object' while the shipped test (session-start.js:114) is positional (a clause whose first token, optionally after and|then|also, is a verb). The C2/C3 VERB LISTS are verbatim in both directions, so the R3 acceptance item itself is met.
findings.requiredFix: Transcribe C1 exactly and restate C3 as 'a clause whose FIRST token, optionally after and|then|also, is an action verb'. Pin-only; no code change.

I re-ran that file on the measured revision: 13 pass / 0 fail. Scope caveat: it proves sensitivity to that repair, NOT coverage of the class — F-4 is a live member of the same class on the decision side and is outside the V1 test set.

optionAJudgement.doesOptionAStillHold: Formally yes; empirically it is calibrated in the wrong direction for the measured population and the data needed to retune it does not exist yet.
facts: 0 of 20 real prompts trigger under the post-R3 tables (session-start 0/5, follow-up 0/15); my A/B shows R3 contributed none of those zeros, and the probe's control (frozen complex #1/#3 trigger, simple 3/3 silent) plus my independent re-derivation rule out a broken probe.

The richest session-start prompt - an explicit alignment ask naming several targets and asking for auto-invocation on complex tasks - produced ZERO signals (1 distinct B verb vs 4; 1 distinct C2 verb vs 3): the observed failure is a MISS, not an over-trigger.
latinOnly = 0 in the dataset, so the English trigger rate is undefined (n=0) and the bilingual claim is unsupported (recorded as the t39 F2 finding in team-compaction-contract.json:55).
The session-start stratum is 5 samples, so its 95% false-positive bound is about 46%: 0/20 cannot distinguish 'well calibrated' from 'dormant' on the positive side.
Option A's stated accepted cost (ordinary multi-clause instruction lists routing) is real but unobserved on this population, and R3 widened exactly that class by one verb.
executableRecommendation: 1. Build a positive stratum first: >= 10 real COMPLEX session-start prompts. A gate that never fires cannot be calibrated by counting false positives; today's evidence only bounds the false-positive rate from above.
2. Fix the English coverage before any cross-language comparison: add English prompts to the recalibration set or drop the bilingual claim.

3. Only then re-tune, cheapest-change-first: C3 (positional clause opening) is the sub-signal most likely to match real multi-step asks - relaxing it to verb-with-object, or lowering ACTION_VERB_MIN from 3 to 2, raises recall on the missed class; each candidate must be re-run through the two-sided gate on BOTH strata with the negative control disarmed.
4. Do NOT touch the C 2-of-3 majority or the signals >= 1 trigger in the same pass: those are what would start routing ordinary prompts and they carry the only measured cost.
5. Record R3's new boundary (the two counterexamples above) in the accepted-cost text, which currently names only the pre-R3 class, so the ledger describes the surface that actually ships.

topRegressionRisk.why: R1 exists to make the clear reachable, so the next change wires it - and that change turns a correct-looking primitive into repeated empty prompts to members whose messages were already read. It is invisible in headless QA because the delivered case asserts the clear's own contract (readMailbox/readLiveMailbox) and never asks the scheduler's reader what it would deliver.
prevention: Filter tombstone !== true inside readUnreadMailbox (or in deliverableUnread).
Keep or re-derive the read/claimed markers on the tombstone so an acknowledged record cannot become unread again.
Add the seam assertion 'cleared mailbox => deliverableUnread(readUnreadMailbox(...)) is empty' to test/r1-message-channel.test.mjs (two lines; it fails today).

Second order: fix the comments that describe unwired behaviour (scheduler.js:230-231, state.js:643-645) in the same change that fixes F-1/F-2 - they read as specifications and will mislead the next implementer.
